title: Sentinel fabric for safe Optimize auto-apply: pressure tests, operator latches, and approval choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a 'sentinel fabric' that enables safe, automated application of Optimize recommendations (batching and KV caching configs) with integrated pressure-testing, operator latches, canary traffic shapes, and approval choreography. This ticket covers the control-plane orchestration, runtime probes, policy evaluation, and audit trail needed for a production-grade auto-apply feature that minimizes regression risk while realizing cost savings automatically.

Goals:
- Provide an automated path for low-risk suggestions to be applied end-to-end without manual intervention.
- Enforce multi-signal safety checks (latency, error rate, model quality on prompt set, and cost delta) before commit.
- Ensure human-in-the-loop for medium/high risk cases via operator latch + explicit approvals.
- Offer auditable rollback and forensic telemetry so SRE/SEs can reason about incidents.

Scope / What this ticket includes:
- Policy engine module that computes a safety_score from telemetry streams and eval metrics. Score components: 95p latency, p99 latency, error rate, regenerated token quality delta on a representative eval set, and expected cost delta.
- Canary runner capable of routing either percent-based traffic or qps-capped traffic to canary variant for N minutes, with traffic shaping presets (conservative, standard, aggressive).
- Pressure-test harness: synthetic prefix priming + KV-cache warmup to emulate steady-state token distribution relevant to the customer's workload class.
- Operator latch: a control-plane hold that can (a) block auto-commit, (b) require manual acknowledge from operator(s), or (c) enable auto-commit after a time-limited grace period.
- Approval choreography: automated approvals for safety_score <= green threshold; 1 PM + 1 SRE approval required for amber; explicit Exec/Customer approval for red or >X% customer-impact.
- Rollback heuristics: automatic rollback triggers on 3-sigma+ deviations on 95p latency, or quality regression > 2% on the eval prompt set, or increased error rate above policy threshold.
- Audit log entries and signed commit events (linkable to KMS keys) for compliance.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
1) Policy engine outputs a reproducible safety_score for a candidate config and stores the evaluation with a trace ID.
2) Canary runner can be invoked with either percent-of-requests or fixed-qps shapes and completes a canary window with telemetry exported to Grafana.
3) Pressure-test harness can replay customer-like prefixes and demonstrates KV-cache warmup prior to canary evaluation.
4) For a low-risk suggestion (synthetic test case provided), the system completes end-to-end auto-apply without manual approvals and provides a signed audit record.
5) For an amber-risk suggestion, the operator latch blocks commit and an approval workflow is generated (notification + approval endpoints), and the action is only applied after the required approvals.
6) Automated rollback triggers and roll back a canary that breaches safety thresholds in a simulated chaos test.
7) Documentation: runbook for on-call, design doc (Confluence), and a QA checklist are published and linked from the ticket.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered so far:
- Safety signals vs cost of false negatives: We prioritize latency and quality signals over short-term cost gains. Conservative thresholds reduce realized savings but limit customer impact.
- Traffic shapes: percent-based canaries are easier to reason about for PLG customers; qps-limited canaries are safer for high-variance tail workloads. We'll support both with conservative default presets.
- Operator UX: prefer operator latches that support single-click acknowledge + optional 'reason' to reduce friction for operations. Still need an approval audit trail.
- Eval prompt set maintenance: using a small, curated signal set per-customer (subset of customer-owned prompts) gives faster feedback but requires onboarding; initial MVP will ship with Redwood-curated workloads mapped to customer archetypes.

Testing plan / QA:
- Unit tests for policy scoring and threshold evaluation.
- Integration tests that spin up a canary runner against a local runtime mock and assert metric deltas and rollback behavior.
- Synthetic workload runs in staging that use the pressure-test harness and validate KV-cache effectiveness and cost delta calculations.
- Chaos testing: introduce artificial latency spikes and packet loss during a canary window to validate rollback and alerting.

Telemetry and observability:
- New Grafana dashboard: optimize.sentinal.canary-{canary_id} with panels for latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, cost delta, eval-quality delta, and safety_score trend.
- Traces: every auto-apply attempt must be correlated with a trace ID and have a link in the audit record.
- Alerts: SRE will get page for critical rollback events; PM and SRE will be notified for amber approvals.

Security and compliance:
- Signed commit events will be KMS-signed and stored in audit logs.
- Rollback artifacts must include the previous config digest and a short rationale for revert (auto or manual).

Links to current artifacts (drafts):
- Confluence design draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Sentinel+Fabric+Design+Draft (private)
- Pressure-test harness prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-pressure-test/pulls/12
- Initial Grafana dashboard (staging): https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/optimize-canary/optimize-canary-staging
- UX mock for operator latch: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcExampleLATCH/view

Next steps (short term):
- Finalize policy scoring weights with Research (meeting 2026-02-28).
- Implement basic canary runner API and pressure-test harness prototype (spike: 2 days).
- Add safety_score export to telemetry stream and wire into dashboard.
- Draft runbook for on-call rollback handling.

Risks:
- False sense of safety if eval prompt set is not representative; mitigation: conservative defaults and require customer opt-in for wider autoapply.
- Increased complexity in control plane; mitigation: incremental rollout of features and strong observability.

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for this ticket):
- ML-driven policy tuning using historical rollouts and labeled regressions.
- Per-customer dynamic thresholds that adapt to seasonality of workload.
- Integration with Dedicated capacity autoscaling to avoid canary-induced capacity pressure.
